items.title: 73243_Joe Thomas oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Bessie Smith in the context of records featuring Louis Armstrong; the interviewee (Joe Thomas) does not respond with any personal anecdote or confirmation of meeting her, only acknowledging the interviewer's statement about the era and musicians.

ctx.x: I don't see why we shouldn't, Stanley. You got it on, you got it off, huh? I don't see why we shouldn't. I think it might have happened during that time, Stan, because I'm beginning to get a chance to get acquainted with the cornet.
But, also I mean what I really meant was on records like Bessie Smith and Nomie Smith, etc., I mean they would be having these people like Joe Smith, Louis Armstrong, probably too.

Well, let me tell you about that. That's another part of the story. That's the reason I don't want to leave Webster Groves, you know. And, Joe Smith, beautiful trumpet player, you know, as you know .... And, Pops, always called Louis Armstrong, he was tremendous. And I think possibly the greatest horn (?) I've heard and a great guy. And ... I've got some funny stories to tell about Pops.
